# Summary of the Scottish National Party Manifesto 1997

## Introduction and Core Message
The 1997 SNP Manifesto, titled "Yes We Can — Win the Best for Scotland," presented the party's case for Scottish independence at the General Election. Led by Alex Salmond, the SNP challenged what it characterized as a "sterile, out of date and bankrupt" British political system, asserting that Scotland had contributed £27 billion more to London than it received since 1979.

## The Case for Independence
The manifesto argued that Scotland is a wealthy nation capable of self-governance. It refuted ten key myths about independence, asserting that Scotland would automatically become an EU member, maintain open borders with England, and establish a modern constitution with full citizenship rights for residents. The SNP proposed that following election of a majority of SNP MPs, independence negotiations would begin, culminating in a referendum.

## Constitutional Proposals
An independent Scotland would feature a written constitution and Bill of Rights protecting human rights including free expression, housing, education, healthcare, and decent working conditions. A single-chamber parliament elected by proportional representation would replace Westminster's "archaic" system, with voting extended to 16-year-olds.

## Economic Policy
The SNP promised significant business tax reforms including cutting corporation tax from 33% to 30%, reducing small company rates from 23% to 18%, and abolishing Class IV National Insurance Contributions. They budgeted £250 million annually for business tax reduction and projected creation of 100,000 new jobs.

For personal taxation, they proposed a 15% starter rate, expanding basic rate bands by 15%, and removing the ceiling on National Insurance contributions—resulting in tax reductions for 85% of male and 95% of female employees.

## Social Justice
Key social proposals included increasing Child Benefit to £12.50 weekly, restoring benefits to 16-17 year olds, and implementing a "Pensioner's Package" with £3-5 weekly pension increases, a Cold Climate Allowance, and abolishing means testing for elderly care. The NHS would receive additional £35 million annually after abolishing the internal market.

## Education, Housing, and Local Services
Education commitments included employing 700 additional teachers, free nursery education for 3-4 year olds, and restoring student grants to 1990 levels. The housing crisis would be addressed by transferring 75% of local authority housing debt to central government, releasing £1.6 billion for investment and enabling construction of 20,000 affordable homes.

## Rural Scotland and Energy
The manifesto proposed land reform including abolishing feudal tenure, supporting agriculture and fishing industries with better EU representation, and phasing out nuclear power generation while developing renewable energy sources.

## Defense and International Relations
Scotland would establish independent defense forces totaling approximately 56,000 personnel, withdraw nuclear weapons, and negotiate phased withdrawal from NATO while maintaining international cooperation through the EU, UN, and other organizations. Overseas aid would increase toward the UN target of 0.7% GDP.

## Financial Framework
A fully costed four-year budget projected debt repayment of £6.6 billion while funding all proposals through Scotland's "relative fiscal surplus" with the UK, employment growth savings, and defense program changes.
